sampling-distribution.def: The sampling distribution of a statistic is the distribution of the values it takes in all possible random samples of the same size from the same population. Its spread shows sampling variability: how much the statistic changes from sample to sample. For the sample mean, $\mu_{\bar{x}} = \mu$ and $\sigma_{\bar{x}} = \frac{\sigma}{\sqrt{n}}$.

clt.def: The Central Limit Theorem says that when the sample size n is large, the sampling distribution of the sample mean is approximately normal, whatever the shape of the population. A common guide is n of 30 or more; if the population is normal, $\bar{x}$ is normal for any n.
